A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 23-page versions of LegalSearchLM, including Appendices A-D. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original legal-case retrieval experiments in Tables 3-4 and difficulty, identifier-ablation, and generalization results in Figures 5-6.

after.justification: v2 retains those original retrieval experiments and supplementary results, including Tables 3-4 and Figures 5-6.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.2 retain the same legal-element extraction, first-token-aware supervision, self-supervised training, and FM-index-constrained beam decoding. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Korean LEGAR BENCH Standard and Stricter coverage: 411 crime types across 33 categories and 160 types across eight categories, respectively. The unseen-crime evaluation scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains BM25, Contriever, and SAILER; Table 4 retains KELLER as a reranking reference. Figure 6 preserves the same naive-identifier comparator and LegalSearchLM training variants.

E3.justification: The P@5 metric, corpus and query sizes, training configurations, and sexual-crime-only generalization setup remain identical. Appendix A.1 also retains the qualification that KELLER uses a different reranking setup.

E4.justification: Figures 5-6 preserve the same analysis by number of matching factors, identifier ablation, and generalization to unseen crime types. No robustness analysis, ablation, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 states in both versions that all results come from single-run experiments. Neither version adds seed information, repeated runs, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 3-4 and Figures 5-6 retain their results. For example, Table 3's LegalSearchLM total P@5 remains 0.68 for Standard and 0.35 for Stricter. No numerical corrections or additional findings appear.

T1.justification: The relevance definitions in Section 2 and constrained-decoding equations (1)-(2) in Section 3.2 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about the Korean benchmark, legal-element generation, advantages over baselines, and generalization to unseen crime types.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning embedding information loss, lexical matching, and legal-element generalization are unchanged. Section 8 retains the Korean-jurisdiction limitation and possible annotation noise from the absence of case-by-case expert verification.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains mT5-base training on 170K cases for one epoch, eight A100 80GB GPUs, and the same baseline implementation settings. Data-processing, repository, annotation-instruction, and licensing disclosures are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to legal retrievers and generative retrieval remain unchanged. The ligature change in Zhijing Wu's name in the Caseformer reference does not change the cited work.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1, 28 May 2025, to v2, 24 September 2025, and an author-name ligature is normalized in one reference. The substantive prose, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Small vertical-spacing adjustments appear in Appendix C and Table 29. Figures and tables retain their content, captions, structure, and placement; none are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the same scientific argument, experimental evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information. The stamp, reference typography, and slight spacing changes do not materially improve or impair the paper's clarity or scientific quality.
